description: 5 should-trigger + 5 should-not-trigger queries. Should-trigger covers running the on-demand jscpd/scanoss similarity scan on a diff or path, and asking whether a diff looks copied from known OSS. Should-not-trigger covers near-miss neighbours (a single named-source license check, notices regeneration, generic code review, dependency vetting) whose vocabulary overlaps.

queries.q: this diff looks suspiciously similar to something I've seen, run a similarity scan against known OSS
run jscpd and scanoss on this PR to check for copied code
do a self-audit of the whole repo for potential license violations
check whether this file matches anything in the SCANOSS knowledge base
the reviewer flagged this function as possibly lifted from elsewhere, scan for a match
I want to borrow this specific function from https://github.com/example/repo, check its license
queries.note: single named source, targeted license check → license-compliance-borrow-check

queries.q: regenerate the third-party notices file from the ledger
review this diff for null-safety and edge cases
queries.note: correctness review, not a similarity scan

queries.q: is this new npm package real or a hallucinated name?
set up a CI job that blocks merges on copied code
queries.note: no CI gate exists or is planned here — Gate G0 cancelled it; this skill is on-demand only
